history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: Bhimeswar Dham is NOT in Tinsukia - it stands at Dakini Pahar (Daini Pahar), Pamohi, near Deepor Beel in Guwahati, Kamrup district, roughly 500 km from Tinsukia. Documented with the corrected location. Legend says Shiva incarnated here to destroy the demon Bhimasura; the Shiva Purana and Koti Rudra Samhita references to Bhimashankar on Dakini hill are interpreted by devotees as this site, so it is locally treated as a Dwadas Jyotirlinga - a claim not counted among the widely recognised twelve (Bhimashankar near Pune is also claimed). There is no formal temple building: the linga sits in a hill stream with water flowing over it continuously, reached by a trek through forest and bamboo groves; a Ganesh temple stands halfway up. The approach road has been renovated recently.

name: Bhimeswar Dham
town: Pamohi, Guwahati (CSV town 'Tinsukia' is WRONG - the dham is at Dakini Pahar, Pamohi, in Guwahati, ~500 km away)
town_description: Pamohi is a semi-rural locality on the southwestern outskirts of Guwahati, beside Deepor Beel (a Ramsar wetland) and the Dakini hill range. Guwahati is Assam's largest city and its main pilgrim hub, home to the Kamakhya Temple.

travel.airport: Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi Airport, Guwahati - about 25 km (verify).
travel.road: About 10-14 km from central Guwahati via NH-37 to Pamohi, then a forest trek (verify).
